sermon.title: My Faith: The Shape of Faith
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Continuing “My Faith,” Pastor David G. Kincer shows from Genesis 18:19 and Job 19 that knowing God—not mere belief—shaped Abraham’s and Job’s character and endurance. From 1 John, John 16 and Hosea 6 he teaches knowing God as a goal beyond basics, warns against celebrity substitutes for Scripture, and closes with Daniel 11:32: people who know their God shall be strong and do great exploits.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: He cites “Job 11” when describing Job as blameless; the wording matches Job 1:1 (linked). “Fear of God is to depart from evil” matches Proverbs 8:13 (quoted_only). New-covenant “all shall know him” is Hebrews 8:11 / Jeremiah 31:34 (quoted_only). Named teachers (Robert Schuller, Creflo Dollar) and criticism of Purpose Driven / prosperity / mass prophecy kept as spoken. Homosexual-altered Bible remark kept as spoken.

chunks.section_question: Do you need apologetics and positive-thinking systems if you know God?
chunks.short_answer: Under the new covenant all shall know him from least to greatest. When you know God you do not need apologetics over crow-count debates, nor positive thinking, Possibility Thinking, Purpose Driven or prosperity psychology—Job stood because he knew God. chunks.section_question: How does knowing God change prayer, worship and assembling?
chunks.short_answer: When you know God you pray, worship, lift hands and assemble because the Master said to—not Simon-says religion or staying away over hurt feelings. You come as a participator to seek him, build the church and share Jesus.

chunks.section_question: What happens to people who know their God (Daniel 11:32)?
chunks.short_answer: Daniel 11:32: the people who know their God shall be strong and do great exploits. The requirement is knowing God; the benefit is strength like Job, Abraham and Paul—you will not quit, and knowing him drives right speech and living.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Those who do wickedly against the covenant he shall corrupt with flattery; but the people who know their God shall be strong, and carry out great exploits.

faqs.question: Did Job say he believed or that he knew?
faqs.answer: He emphasizes Job said “I know,” not “I believe” or “I have faith,” about his Redeemer living.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For I know that my Redeemer lives, And He shall stand at last on the earth;

faqs.question: Should Christians rely on bookstore books instead of the Bible?
faqs.answer: He says America’s trouble is putting faith in Christian bookstore books and megachurch tapes instead of this Book; God can talk to you if you read and study.

faqs.question: What is the fear of God in Job’s life?
faqs.answer: He says the fear of God is to depart from evil, and Job hated and shunned evil because he knew God.

faqs.question: Whom should believers hear according to 1 John 4:6?
faqs.answer: He who knows God hears the apostles; America listens to every Tom, Dick and Harry claiming revelation instead of James, Paul and Jesus.

scriptures.text_nkjv: We are of God. He who knows God hears us; he who is not of God does not hear us. By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

faqs.question: How do we know the spirit of truth versus the spirit of error?
faqs.answer: By this we know: sticking with the apostles’, Jesus’ and the prophets’ doctrine is the spirit of truth; listening to celebrity teachers instead of the Scriptures enters the spirit of error.

scriptures.text_nkjv: We are of God. He who knows God hears us; he who is not of God does not hear us. By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

faqs.question: Is blaming the church or America the real problem?
faqs.answer: He says when we blame our church or America we are lying—we lack knowing God, or we would try to pick America and the church back up.

faqs.question: Must you follow on after being saved to know the Lord?
faqs.answer: From Hosea 6, after returning to the Lord you know if you follow on to know the Lord—yes, after salvation and water baptism you must follow on.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Let us know, Let us pursue the knowledge of the LORD. His going forth is established as the morning; He will come to us like the rain, Like the latter and former rain to the earth.

faqs.question: Is lining up a whole congregation for personal prophecy scriptural?
faqs.answer: He says they were at a meeting where everyone would be prophesied over, and that is not scriptural; Jesus taught the word to the multitudes.

faqs.question: Why assemble if someone at church hurt you?
faqs.answer: Because the Master said assemble together all the more as you see the day approaching, provoking one another to love and good works—you come to seek him and build, not over who smiled.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

faqs.question: What is the benefit of knowing God in Daniel 11:32?
faqs.answer: They shall be strong and do great exploits—you will not shake or quit; love never quits.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Those who do wickedly against the covenant he shall corrupt with flattery; but the people who know their God shall be strong, and carry out great exploits.
